title: A morning in Johari Bazaar
excerpt: Pink arches, chai at 9 a.m., and the tray of antique-gold kadas that became our Rajwada Kada.
author: Nemara Buying Team

cover.alt: Rajwada Kada pair on a stone plinth

body.text: We get to Johari Bazaar before ten, which in Jaipur means most shutters are still half down. That's the best time: owners have time to talk, and the trays haven't been picked over yet.
Red, green… and a few tiny bells

Most counters here lead with the same bright bridal sets. Three shops in, the owner of a small workshop brought out a tray of antique-gold kadas — carved florals, red and green stones, and tiny ghungroos that chime when you move. That tray became our Rajwada Kada.
We asked for one change: a smooth hinge, so it opens and closes without a struggle. Two weeks later, the samples arrived — and the matching temple necklace came with them.
Out of every fifty pieces we pick up in a market, one makes it to Nemara.
What we look for in Jaipur
Crisp carving, stones that sit flush, finishes that look rich up close — and pieces light enough to wear from the haldi to the reception.

title: How we check every piece before it reaches you
excerpt: Plating, stones, clasps, weight, edges — the checklist every Nemara find has to pass.
author: Nemara Quality Desk

cover.alt: Close-up of the Jaali Bloom AD kada

body.text: Markets are where the magic is. They're also where quality varies the most. So nothing goes from a market tray straight into your bag — every piece comes through our checking table first.

Plating: checked under bright light for patches and bubbles. Stones and pearls: pushed, twisted and matched in pairs. Clasps and hooks: opened and closed until we trust them. Weight: earrings have to be comfortable for a full evening. Edges: every part that touches skin should feel smooth.
If a piece fails, it goes back. If a whole batch fails, we drop the design — however pretty it is.
Market finds, checked like fine jewellery. And backed by a 3-month warranty.
Then it's packed in a Nemara pouch with a card that tells you which market it came from — so your piece arrives with its story.

title: One bangle, five versions of you
excerpt: The Starline Stone Bangle, worn from a Monday stand-up to a Saturday sangeet.
author: Nemara Studio

cover.alt: Starline Stone Bangle worn with a chikankari kurta

body.text: Monday: the Starline bangle alone, crisp white shirt, sleeves pushed up. One line of light does the talking.
Wednesday: stack it with the Cupid's Arrow Bracelet, watch on the other wrist. Balanced, not matched.
Friday: add the Blush Bamboo Bracelet. A little pink, a little play.
Saturday: with a silk saree and the Petal Drop Earrings — gold to gold, soft to sparkle.
Sunday: lend it to your sister. She'll know why.
